newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG-Caltex targets max output on CDU by late Dec.
newsitem.headline: LG-Caltex targets max output on CDU by late Dec.

text.p: South Korea's LG-Caltex Oil Corp, a unit of LG Group, said on Tuesday it expected full commercial production at its new crude distillation unit (CDU) by late December.
The new CDU has a government licensed production capacity of 220,000 barrels per day (bpd), but company officials said the unit will be capable of processing 270,000 bpd of crude oil.
"We plan to start test-running in mid-December and run the new unit commercially in late December," said a spokesman for LG-Caltex.
He said the company would go through final checks in the meantime.

However, a company official at Yeochon refinery previously told Reuters that LG-Caltex was postponing a crude feed which was set for November 16 due to a defect in the topper's column. He added LG-Caltex was also delaying full production of the unit, which was scheduled for November 23.
The spokesman declined to confirm the report.
"Everything is going as officially planned," he said.
The new unit will boost LG-Caltex's licensed crude processing capacity to 600,000 bpd from the current 380,000 bpd to become the country's second largest refiner.
South Korea currently has a refining capability of 2.22 million bpd.
LG-Caltex is a joint venture between LG Group and Caltex Petroleum Corp, itself a joint venture between U.S. oil giants Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
